verdict.headline: Rates broke from oil on Friday; Xi-Trump summit and August PCE lead next week
verdict.label: Week close: S&P 500 7,650.50 (+0.17% Fri, ~flat for week); Nasdaq +2.6% wk, Dow -1.7% wk; 10Y 5.006% rose while WTI fell 1.6% to $100.30 Friday — first session this month they moved apart; DXY 100.3; BTC $81,298 Saturday
verdict.rationale_short:
The week's headline number was the Federal Reserve's first rate hike in three years. On Wednesday September 16 the committee raised its target range by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.00% unanimously, with 16 of 18 officials projecting at least one further increase this year and four projecting two. Futures markets price about 4.2% by December and 4.7% by September 2027, putting two additional moves in the market's consensus behind the one already delivered.

What the week also illustrated is a driver shift. From September 10's pipeline attack through Wednesday, the long end of the Treasury curve moved with crude — the attack lifted both, Aramco's restoration progress pulled both lower. Thursday and Friday broke that pattern. WTI fell 1.6% Friday to settle at $100.30, declining for a third straight session as Saudi Arabia works to restore about half the East-West pipeline's 4-5 million barrel-a-day capacity within days and full capacity in roughly six weeks. The ten-year yield rose six basis points to 5.006% regardless, back above the 5% it gave up Thursday. The two-year also rose five basis points to 4.743%, and the thirty-year four to 5.336%. A whole-curve parallel shift that leads from the front end is the signature of a market pricing the federal funds rate, not a supply-shock premium leaving the oil price.

The S&P 500 added 0.17% Friday to 7,650.50 and ended the week roughly flat. The Nasdaq gained 0.39% Friday and 2.6% for the week, carried by large-cap growth. The Dow fell 95 points on Friday and 1.7% for the week — a divergence that maps onto duration: long-dated growth assets held, rate-sensitive value and small-caps did not. The VIX settled at 14.81, down 4.08%, in the same session that removed roughly $7 trillion of options notional — the second-largest quarterly triple witching on record — with about 60% clearing at the open. Monday is the first session the index trades without the positioning that has been absorbing directional pressure.

Two secondary stories carry into next week. The SEC's five-year conditional Innovation Exemption for tokenized stock venues cleared Thursday, allowing qualifying platforms to trade tokenized US-listed stocks without exchange registration, subject to caps on symbols and volume. Bitcoin reclaimed $80,000 and is trading at $81,298 Saturday on Crypto.com exchange data; Coinbase closed 11.53% near $194. Volkswagen cut its 2026 margin guidance to at most 1% from 4.0%-5.5% on EUR 10 billion of one-off items, roughly EUR 6 billion a Porsche impairment, citing US tariffs and collapsing Chinese demand for foreign luxury brands; the DAX fell 1.65% and European indices roughly 1.5%.

The evidence is not one-directional. Gold rose 1.00% Friday to $4,384.78, with silver up 2.01%, while nominal yields also rose across the entire curve — metals rising alongside rising yields is consistent with the move being priced as inflation compensation rather than a higher real rate. And one session after a record expiry is a narrow base for declaring a driver change; the yield-oil decoupling needs another session to confirm.

Three tests arrive in the week ahead. S&P Global Flash PMIs on Tuesday give the first read on September's economic health after the hike. Xi Jinping's White House visit Wednesday through Thursday is the largest bilateral event in years: the two sides are discussing about $30 billion in tariff cuts, including China's 15% levy on U.S. LNG and expanded agricultural purchase commitments. Tariff relief on U.S. LNG at a moment when oil is the cited rationale for further Fed hikes would reduce one energy-import cost and complicate the inflation story in one move. August PCE on Friday is the Fed's preferred inflation measure and the last major data point before the November meeting. August core CPI ran a tenth above consensus at 0.3%; PCE weights shelter differently from CPI, and shelter was the hot line. A PCE core at or under 0.2% weakens the case for a November hike; at or above 0.3% it strengthens it.

What would change the reading: a WTI settle below $100 while the ten-year retreats toward Thursday's 4.949% close would say Friday's decoupling was the record expiry talking rather than a change of driver. A ten-year that holds above Wednesday's 5.016% intra-week high as crude continues lower says the rate level is now priced on the Fed path alone. On the diplomatic front, binding tariff announcements from the Xi-Trump summit change the energy inflation setup; a summit that produces only a joint statement does not.
verdict.lede_short: The ten-year rose six basis points to 5.006% Friday while WTI fell 1.6% to $100.30 for a third straight session — the first day this month they moved apart — with the whole curve rising in parallel, pricing the Fed rather than oil. Three catalysts follow: Flash PMIs Tuesday, Xi Jinping at the White House with $30 billion in tariff cuts on the table Wednesday-Thursday, and August PCE on Friday. A ten-year retreat to Thursday's 4.949% as oil continues lower would say the decoupling was Friday's record expiry talking; a hold above 5.016% says the energy-rates link is broken.

The $100 level is the regime threshold, and WTI is 30 cents above it. The change from the prior two weeks is that crude fell on Friday and the ten-year rose anyway, which is the first session this month the two moved in opposite directions.

trade_setups.thesis: Xi Jinping's White House visit is the week's highest-stakes event. The U.S. and China are in active discussion on about $30 billion in tariff cuts, including potential removal of China's 15% levy on U.S. LNG and expanded agricultural purchase commitments on top of the 25 million ton soybean pledge already in place. Both sides built the framework for these talks at the May Beijing summit, where they established the US-China Board of Trade and a parallel Board of Investment. A state dinner is scheduled for September 24. LNG tariff relief would lower import costs for U.S. energy buyers at the precise moment energy pass-through is the Fed's cited rationale for further hikes — a supply-side disinflationary event the market would need to price into the November rate path in real time. The counter-evidence is that state visits frequently produce governance language rather than binding terms, and the May framework has yet to deliver a specific tariff schedule. Volkswagen's warning last week — cutting 2026 margin guidance to at most 1% from 4.0%-5.5% while citing US tariffs and collapsing Chinese demand — is sitting in European markets as the established cost of the current tariff regime.
trade_setups.entry: DAX at approximately 25,309 and S&P 500 at 7,650.50 entering the week, with VW and Porsche down 5.6% and 3.3% on the tariff-demand channel. A summit producing binding tariff cuts on energy and agriculture reads into autos, industrials, and agricultural exporters.
trade_setups.invalidation: A summit that produces only a joint statement or a governance communiqué leaves the Volkswagen demand channel intact and removes the disinflationary input from the Fed's November calculus.

trade_setups.asset: August PCE — Friday September 26, 8:30 a.m. ET
trade_setups.thesis: August PCE is the Fed's preferred inflation measure and the last significant data release before the November FOMC meeting. The committee raised to 3.75%-4.00% last week with 16 of 18 officials projecting at least one more hike. August core CPI ran a tenth hot at 0.3%, with the shelter index accelerating to 0.3% from 0.1% — shelter is roughly a third of core CPI but carries a smaller weight in PCE, so PCE can print below CPI on the same underlying data. A core PCE at or under 0.2% with the ten-year retreating from 5% would support the one-and-done interpretation the dot plot resisted; a reading at or above 0.3% puts the second hike squarely in play for November. This reading arrives after, and potentially colored by, whatever comes out of the Xi-Trump summit Wednesday-Thursday.
trade_setups.entry: Ten-year at 5.006%, with Wednesday's intra-week high of 5.016% as the level above that would mark a new cycle high on a hot PCE print.
trade_setups.invalidation: A PCE core print at or under 0.2% that pulls the ten-year back toward Thursday's 4.949% would say one hike was sufficient and the data supports a November hold.

trade_setups.thesis: The S&P 500 gained 0.17% Friday in a session where roughly $7 trillion of options notional expired — the second-largest quarterly triple witching on record — with about 60% clearing at the open. Quarterly expiries are widely modelled scheduled events; the last several have passed without a change in market regime. But the VIX's Friday reading of 14.81 was measured while the buffer that has been absorbing directional moves was still in place. The S&P 500 is 150 points above the 7,500 regime threshold. A hold above 7,500 through Monday with the VIX remaining roughly below 17 would say the calm was not primarily positioning-dependent. A break of 7,500 in the first sessions without the expiry would say it was.
trade_setups.entry: 7,650.50 on the S&P 500, VIX at 14.81, as the reference for what was priced with the expiry still in place.
trade_setups.invalidation: A hold above 7,500 through Tuesday with no new macro shock says the expiry transition was orderly.
trade_setups.horizon: Monday-Tuesday, the first two sessions without expiry positioning
